paper.title: Risk-Averse Explore-Then-Commit Algorithms for Finite-Time Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: One-time exploitation MAB after an experimentation phase (OTE-MAB)
unmapped: target arm maximises p_k = P(R_k >= all other arms' rewards), not the mean
goal: return arm with p_{k*} - p_{khat} < Delta p with probability >= 1 - eps_r (PAC-style on the win-probability criterion)
each arm sampled exactly N times (uniform exploration); if arm rewards are dependent, all arms are observed simultaneously in each experiment
arm reward distributions arbitrary with finite means
settings.definition_quote: Consider arms $\mathcal{K} = \{1, 2, \dots, K\}$ whose rewards are random variables $R_1, R_2, \dots, R_K$ that have unknown distributions $f_1, f_2, \dots, f_K$ ... The finite-time exploitation regret ... $r_M(\Delta p) = P ( p_{k^*}^M - p_{\hat{k}}^M \geq \Delta p )$.

settings.name_in_paper: One-time exploitation MAB with knowledge of Delta p^*
unmapped: target arm maximises p_k = P(R_k >= all other arms' rewards); goal is to identify it exactly (P(khat != k*) < eps_r)
learner knows a lower bound on Delta p^* = p_(1) - p_(2), the gap in win probabilities (not in means)
each arm sampled exactly N times; simultaneous observation if arms dependent
settings.definition_quote: Having the knowledge of $\Delta p^*$ or a lower bound on it, a stronger notion of regret can be defined as $r = \inf_{\Delta p > 0} r(\Delta p) = P ( \hat{k} \neq k^* )$

settings.name_in_paper: Finite-time (M-time) exploitation MAB after an experimentation phase (FTE-MAB)
unmapped: target arm maximises p_k^M = P(R_k^M >= all others), R_k^M the sum of M i.i.d. draws of arm k
learner knows the number of exploitations M
goal: p_{k*}^M - p_{khat}^M < Delta p with probability >= 1 - eps_r
each arm sampled exactly N times; simultaneous observation if arms dependent
settings.definition_quote: The goal is to identify the best arm at the end of an experimentation phase that is followed by an exploitation phase, where the best arm is exploited for a given number of times, $M < \infty$. ... $k^* = \argmax_k P(R_k^M \geq \boldsymbol{R}_{-k}^M)$

settings.name_in_paper: Finite-time exploitation MAB with knowledge of Delta p^*_M
unmapped: target arm maximises p_k^M = P(R_k^M >= all others); goal is exact identification P(khat != k*) < eps_r
learner knows M and a lower bound on Delta p^*_M (gap in M-sum win probabilities)
each arm sampled exactly N times; simultaneous observation if arms dependent
settings.definition_quote: Having the knowledge of $\Delta p^*_M$ or a lower bound on it, a stronger notion of regret can be defined as $r_M = \inf_{\Delta p > 0} r_M(\Delta p) = P ( \hat{k} \neq k^* )$

conditions: simultaneous exploration of the K arms if arm rewards are dependent

source.label: theorem1
source.quote: For any $0 < \epsilon_r, \Delta p < 1,$ if each of the $K$ arms are experimented for $N \geq \frac{2 \ln \left ( \frac{2K}{\epsilon_r} \right )}{{\Delta p}^2}$ times in the experimentation phase, the one-time exploitation regret defined in Equation \eqref{regret} is bounded by $\epsilon_r$, i.e. $r(\Delta p) \leq \epsilon_r$. Note that simultaneous exploration of the $K$ arms are required in the experimentation phase if arm rewards are dependent.

results.notes: Bound is on the number of samples N per arm (total K*N). delta = eps_r (failure probability), epsilon = Delta p (accuracy in win probability p_k). 'Regret' is P(p_{k*} - p_{khat} >= Delta p). Compute: the independent-arm estimator sums over N^K tuples (exponential in K); the dependent-arm estimator is linear in N.

symbols.Delta_p_star: gap between the two largest win probabilities p_(1) - p_(2) (or a known lower bound on it)

conditions: learner knows Delta p^* or a lower bound on it
instantaneous exploration of the K arms if arms are dependent

source.quote: From the theoretical point of view, upon the knowledge of $\Delta p^*$ or a lower bound on it, for any $0 < \epsilon_r < 1$, the regret defined in Equation \eqref{regret_optimum} is bounded by $\epsilon_r,$ i.e. $r < \epsilon_r$, if the $K$ arms are explored for $N \geq \frac{2 \ln \left ( \frac{2K}{\epsilon_r} \right )}{{\Delta p^*}^2}$ times each.

results.notes: Per-arm sample count guaranteeing P(khat != k*) < eps_r (delta).

symbols.M_exploit: number of exploitations M after commitment

conditions: simultaneous exploration of the K arms if arm rewards are dependent
tuning: N chosen such that floor(N/M) >= 2 ln(2K/eps_r)/Delta p^2

source.label: theorem2
source.quote: For any $0 < \epsilon_r, \Delta p < 1,$ if each of the $K$ arms is explored for $N$ times in the experimentation phase such that $\lfloor \frac{N}{M} \rfloor \geq \frac{2 \ln \left ( \frac{2K}{\epsilon_r} \right )}{{\Delta p}^2}$, the finite-time exploitation regret defined in Definition \ref{regret_definition} is bounded by $\epsilon_r$, i.e. $r_M(\Delta p) \leq \epsilon_r$.

results.notes: The condition is on floor(N/M); expression records N approximately M times the threshold (exact requirement: floor(N/M) >= 2 ln(2K/eps_r)/Delta p^2). The appendix proof contains a typo (a^2 = K/eps_r). Corollary 3 (M -> infinity recovers max-mean arm) is qualitative and not recorded.

symbols.M_exploit: number of exploitations M after commitment
symbols.Delta_p_star_M: gap between the two largest M-time win probabilities p^M_(1) - p^M_(2) (or a known lower bound)

conditions: learner knows Delta p^*_M or a lower bound on it
instantaneous exploration of the K arms if arms are dependent
tuning: N such that floor(N/M) >= 2 ln(2K/eps_r)/Delta p*_M^2

source.quote: From the theoretical point of view, upon the knowledge of $\Delta p^*_M$ or a lower bound on it, for any $0 < \epsilon_r < 1$, the regret defined in Equation \eqref{regret_optimum_M} is bounded by $\epsilon_r,$ i.e. $r_M < \epsilon_r$, if the $K$ arms are explored for $N$ times each, where $ \lfloor \frac{N}{M} \rfloor \geq \frac{2 \ln \left ( \frac{2K}{\epsilon_r} \right )}{{\Delta p^*_M}^2}$.
